doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Between Bird gigs, Miles in 1951, and Sarah Vaughan's hiring
summary: He worked irregularly, recorded with Miles in 1951, first went to Europe in 1954, and avoided studio work. Her manager George Treadwell had hoped for him since Chicago with Lester Young.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. Let’s backtrack. So you’re already with Bird, doing Bird and strings. So, early ’50s. After you left Bird, or probably while you’re working with Bird, you’re working with some other folks then too.
In between, because we didn’t work steady, steady during that period. Miles used to say then that Bird stole his drummer.
But you ended up recording with Miles in the early ’50s.
’51. You didn’t – your first trip to Europe wasn’t until ’54. Is that correct?

So you’re working mostly small ensemble jazz gigs at this time? You weren’t doing other things. You weren’t doing Broadway shows or any soundtracks, any of those kinds of things. Basically live groups.

No, but after Sarah that almost came about. There was some – a little interest there. The bassist Joe Benjamin, he started going that direction, and I was thinking about it. But I’m glad I didn’t go that direction.
How did you hook up with Sarah? How did that come about?

George Treadwell was her manager. I think we had played – even when I was with Lester Young, we played Chicago for a few weeks. Sarah was there, so I had to accompany her there. He was always hoping from then on that I’d be Sarah’s drummer. And she liked me. I went and did that.
